transcript:
HEADER
Date: 2026-03-15 10:00 AM PT
Duration: ~60 minutes
Attendees (selected): Sarah Lee (CEO), Carlos Ramirez (VP Eng), Priya Patel (Head of Product), Maya Sanchez (Head of Ops), Jonah Kim (Head of Sales), plus all staff.

SUMMARY (auto-generated):
- Quick Q1 review, product milestones, security/compliance update, hiring, OKRs.
- Quick Q&A and open mic at the end.

--- TRANSCRIPT ---
[00:00] Sarah: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, appreciate the on-time start. We'll run about an hour, quick company updates, then leadership updates and Q&A. Lots to cover.
[00:20] Carlos: Quick housekeeping — recording is on, Slack questions in #all-hands. If you're remote, say hi in chat.
[00:35] Sarah: Alright first slide — Q1 highlights. Revenue up vs plan, still early but good trajectory. We're seeing particular momentum on Dedicated and a few large mid-market wins. Jonah will share more on sales in a sec.
[01:05] Jonah: Thanks. Quick numbers — closed three new Dedicated deals in Feb, pipeline healthy. We're seeing longer procurement cycles on Private but customers are committed. Biggest ask from prospects is predictability — consistent latency and cost.
[01:40] Sarah: Good. On product, Priya?
[01:45] Priya: Yep. Product update — API improvements: streaming upgrades, more robust function calling, and better structured output for customers using tools. We're shipping a few SDK updates this month. Dedicated: pilot customers are onboarded, autoscale improvements in canary. Private: on-prem packaging is in validation with two early customers.
[02:20] Priya: Also Optimize is getting a quantization recommendations engine — think recommended q4_8 and batching profiles per route, surfaced in Console.
[02:40] Carlos: On the runtime side — we landed a set of kernel selections that give 12-18% token throughput improvements on Ada-like models on A100/next-gen hardware. There's still work optimizing KV cache behaviour for long context, we've seen some edge cases where the prefix caching doesn't win and we'll tune heuristics.
[03:15] Sarah: Nice. Any risks?
[03:20] Carlos: Capacity constraints remain a focus; forecasting for Dedicated demand is tricky month to month. We're adding better smart routing so low-priority traffic can be shifted to spot pools. Also, small note — the team observed one regression in late-night batching that increased p99 lat slightly; fix is in review.
[03:50] Maya: On ops and reliability — uptime is within SLA for most customers; we had two short incidents related to a scaling policy where autoscaler thrash triggered a fallback. Root cause is mitigations being rolled out.
[04:12] Sarah: Security update, Maya?
[04:15] Maya: SOC 2 progress: control mapping complete, evidence collection 80% done, auditor kickoff scheduled next week. We're also expanding KMS integrations — HSM-backed key storage for Private deployments coming Q2. SSO/SAML improvements and RBAC expansions are in beta for Console.
[04:45] Jonah: Sales note — we need a simple one-pager about security for procurement teams; often procurement asks for SOC 2 and KMS specifics.
[04:55] Maya: We'll make that. I'll send an FAQ pack to the sales team by Thursday.
[05:10] Sarah: Great. Hiring — Priya, People Ops?
[05:15] Priya: We're prioritizing infra, SE, and a couple PM roles. Hiring pipeline is moving but interview no-shows remain an issue; we'll tighten scheduling.
[05:35] People Ops (voice): We're updating the interview panel rubric and will post the schedule.
[05:45] Sarah: Okay let's go into a slightly deeper product demo — Carlos take it away on the Dedicated performance baselines.
[06:00] Carlos: Sure. I'll start with a quick demo — this is a canary dashboard view in Console. Note — these are internal numbers and we'll publish cleaned numbers to the docs soon.
[06:20] [06:20] Carlos: (screen share) Here's throughput under burst, p50/p95/p99 latency curves, and we've got token-per-second improvements after the latest kernel swap. We're also showing per-route batching efficiency — routes with steady short-turnaround traffic see big improvements.
[07:10] Alex (Eng): Quick question — are the numbers with quantization or FP16?
[07:15] Carlos: These are mixed: most are int8 quantized runs on the new exec path, FP16 for larger context runs. The quantization path isn't yet universal; we're doing compatibility checks with a set of open models.
[07:40] Priya: Also note: when we switch to aggressive batching the latency profile for interactive apps can degrade, so Optimize will suggest per-route policies that balance latency SLOs vs cost.
[08:10] Sarah: On the topic of customer pilots — Jonah, who are we running Dedicated pilots with?
[08:20] Jonah: A handful — two mid-market SaaS customers and one enterprise in fintech. We're asking them to sign a short pilot agreement and run benchmarks; SEs will be embedded.
[08:40] Priya: We need to standardize the benchmark harness so it's reproducible and easy to share. Carlos?
[08:50] Carlos: Totally — we're working on a harness that runs on both Dedicated and Hosted so we can show delta and fallback behaviour. Note: some transcriptions say "kay-vee cache" during testing — that's the KV cache.
[09:10] [09:10] Sarah: Quick org updates — we promoted Maya to Head of Ops, congrats. Also we've consolidated two infra teams into runtime and infra orchestration.
[09:35] Maya: Thanks. Ops will run a postmortem on the autoscaler incident and publish the blameless report.
[09:50] Sarah: OK open mic Q&A — please keep questions short.
[10:05] Emily (Product): Are we changing pricing with Dedicated?
[10:10] Jonah: Not yet public; for pilots we'll do discounted reserved rates. We are working with finance on a pricing playbook for net-new customers.
[10:25] Tony (SE): For Private deployments — what are the support SLAs?
[10:30] Maya: We're offering tiered SLAs depending on on-prem vs VPC. On-prem enterprise installs will have a support contract with 24/7 option and runbook access. We'll publish details in the support portal.
[10:50] Priya: Also, Private customers will get HSM/KMS options and audit log shipping — important for regulated customers.
[11:05] Raj (Eng): Any change to model catalog?
[11:10] Priya: We're adding a curated set of smaller open models for embeddings and a set of Redwood-verified RTC models with performance profiles. We'll publish the catalog page next week.
[11:35] Sarah: Question from chat — "When is the next product town hall?" Priya?
[11:40] Priya: We'll run a product town hall in two weeks (March 31) focused on Optimize and Dedicated.
[11:55] Sarah: Great. A couple more quick things — we want better visibility on per-token economics across routes; Console will add a token-cost view for top 10 routes in the next sprint. Carlos will lead that.
[12:15] Carlos: Yep, on it.
[12:20] [12:20] Open mic — short lightning round of wins from teams.
[12:30] Eng team member: We shipped the autoscaler fix to staging and unit tests are green.
[12:45] Sales rep: Closed a mid-market deal with a large marketplace; they were sold on Dedicated's predictability.
[12:55] Security engineer: Completed encryption-at-rest audit for Private customer A.
[13:05] Sarah: Thanks everyone. Quick recap of action items — Priya will share roadmap deck, Carlos will publish perf baselines, Maya will send SOC 2 packet, Jonah to circulate pilot list, People Ops will post hiring prioritization.
[13:30] Sarah: Final Q — anything urgent?
[13:35] Silence/busy typing in chat.
[13:45] Sarah: Alright thank you all. Meeting adjourned.

POST-MEETING NOTES:
- Links shared during the meeting: product roadmap (doc link), canary dashboard (internal link), SOC 2 plan (internal link).
- Recording available in #all-hands-recordings.

- Carlos Ramirez: Publish performance baseline and Console token-cost view by 2026-03-22.
- Maya Sanchez: Distribute SOC 2 evidence packet and compliance FAQ to Sales by 2026-03-19.
- Jonah Kim: Share pilot customer list and pairing details by 2026-03-18.
- People Ops: Post hiring prioritization doc and interview panel details by 2026-03-20.

END OF TRANSCRIPT
